notes: Newly arrived corps (O'Connor, 60,244 men) launched Epsom 26 June from the 3rd Canadian Division beachhead; 736 guns in support; aim to cross Odon and Orne south of Caen.
Odon bridge at Tourmauville seized 27 June (11th Armd); bridgehead across the Odon formed.

Dempsey reinforced the Odon bridgehead with a brigade of 43rd Division and pulled in the perimeter; 29th Armd Bde withdrawn north of the river after dark; II SS Panzer Corps counter-attacked (9th/10th SS).

current_activity: containing German counterattacks as Epsom ended
notes: Operation Epsom ended 30 June: German counter-attacks contained, some forces withdrawn from over the Odon; VIII Corps casualties 26-30 June: 470 killed, 2,187 wounded, 706 missing.

current_activity: Goodwood: the three armoured divisions of VIII Corps lead the advance south from the bridgehead east of the Orne
notes: Event date: 18 July 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, pp. 335, 336). Event definition: VIII Corps strikes south between I Corps and II Canadian Corps with the Guards, 7th and 11th Armoured Divisions: its orders are to establish the divisions in the areas of Vimont, Garcelles-Secqueville and Hubert-Folie and Verrieres so firmly that no enemy can penetrate between them; the three divisions cross the Orne one after another and cannot enter the battle together (p. 335). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 336: "VIII Corps, in the centre, was first to get the main bodies of its armoured divisions so firmly established in the areas of (a) Vimont, (b) Garcelles-Secqueville and (c) Hubert-Folie and Verriéres that there could be no enemy penetration between them, and enemy armour brought against them would be defeated"; p. 335: "the three armoured divisions of VIII Corps which were to lead the advance". Location: Cagny, Calvados (existing place PL0529) with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: the point is Cagny, in the middle of the corps objectives; none of the three areas is the corps headquarters. Location support: Ellis names the three areas but no single corps position; Cagny is the village fought over by the corps in the centre of that front (pp. 341-343). Commander: General O'Connor, VIII Corps (Ellis, vol. I, p. 394).

current_activity: Bluecoat: attacks south from Caumont; its spearheads are five or six miles south of the town by the end of the day

current_activity: Advance to the Elbe: by 8 April a division is across the Leine north of Hanover, 150 miles from the Rhine
notes: Event date: by 8 April 1945 (Ellis, vol. II, pp. 305, 306). Event definition: Second Army's two leading corps drive for the Elbe: by 8 April VIII Corps has a division across the Leine river north of Hanover and its leading troops have advanced roughly a hundred and fifty miles from the Rhine; the corps consisted initially of the 11th Armoured and 6th Airborne Divisions and the 1st Commando Brigade, later joined by the 15th Division and the 6th Guards Armoured Brigade; its leading divisions capture Osnabruck on 4 April and reach the Weser on the 5th; the 11th Armoured Division reaches Emsdetten on 31 March and bridges the Ems and the Dortmund-Ems Canal (pp. 305-306). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 305: "by the 8th, VIII Corps had a division across the Leine river north of Hanover"; "VIII Corps: initially 11th Armoured and 6th Airborne Divisions"; p. 306: "Osna- briick was captured on the 4th and the Weser reached on the 5th". Location: Hannover, Niedersachsen (existing place PL0454), the town beside the Leine crossing with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: the point is Hannover, close to the Leine crossing north of the city; the corps headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis puts the Leine crossing north of Hanover (p. 305); the corps headquarters is not named.

current_activity: Elbe: crosses the Elbe below Lauenburg at 02:00; the 6th Airborne and 11th Armoured Divisions follow on the 30th
notes: Event date: 29 April 1945, 02:00 (Ellis, vol. II, pp. 310, 311, 337). Event definition: VIII Corps crosses the Elbe below Lauenburg on 29 April, the river being 800 to 1,000 feet wide and held by about 6,000 men of low category supported by over 100 guns (note); one brigade of the 15th (Scottish) Division and a Commando brigade assault at 02:00 and the first bridge opens that night; the 6th Airborne Division starts to cross on the afternoon of the 30th and is followed in the evening by the 11th Armoured Division, which has orders to break out to the Baltic; the still intact railway bridge at Lauenburg had become the corps' immediate objective after 11 April, but it was blown (pp. 310 and 337). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 337: "Twenty-First Army Group's VIII Corps had crossed the Elbe below Lauenburg"; "The 6th Airborne Division started to cross the river on the afternoon of the 3oth"; pp. 310-311: "the still intact railway bridge at Lauenburg became VIII Corps' immediate objective". Location: Lauenburg/Elbe, Schleswig-Holstein (existing place PL0658) with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is the town of Lauenburg; the crossing was below it and the corps headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis names the crossing below Lauenburg (p. 337).
